evidence: The released four-A100 H3 workload reports dense 217.32 seconds, full-opt 61.28 seconds, and 3.55x speedup at 1344x768, 124 frames, 50 steps, and seed 0.
The matched four-A800 reproduction measured dense 216.599563 seconds, full-opt 61.683806 seconds, and 3.511449x speedup: -0.33%, +0.66%, and -1.09% respectively versus the released A100 figures.

The A800 optimized benchmark records Triton Sol-Attn on all four ranks, effective route density 0.180392, FirstBlockCache reuse on 33 of 49 calls, and 48098 MiB peak reserved memory per GPU versus 47724 MiB for dense.
The local 64-frame telemetry measured PSNR 16.739925, SSIM 0.676956, and temporal relative error 0.127109.
lessons: The A800 result closely reproduces the released A100 end-to-end acceleration while using the portable SM80 Triton backend.
The 3.511x result belongs to the composed Sol-Attn plus FirstBlockCache profile and cannot be attributed to either component without ablation.
Sol-Engine ranks lossy generative profiles with aligned pairwise Gemini artifact severity and aligned LPIPS rather than a fixed PSNR or SSIM delivery threshold.
limitations: The released A100 H3 profile does not publish a directly comparable PSNR or SSIM value, so the local pixel telemetry cannot quantify a delta against an upstream PSNR or SSIM reference.
The reproduction covers one released prompt and seed on four A800 GPUs; multi-prompt, H100, and component-ablation coverage is separate work.
Generated videos and checkpoints remain outside Git and are referenced by the recorded run directory.
next_actions: Evaluate the same outputs with the upstream aligned LPIPS and pairwise artifact rubric for an apples-to-apples quality comparison.
Run dense, Sol-Attn-only, FirstBlockCache-only, and composed profiles over a fixed multi-prompt robot-action suite.
scope: matched four-A800 MiniMax-H3 dense versus Sol-Engine fullopt_exact inference
summary: The four-A800 H3 full-opt reproduction reached 3.511x versus the released four-A100 3.55x result, a 1.09% relative difference.
